citation: Shao S; Shortt Z; Sulman B; Pries C H (2025): Myco-CORPSE simulations assessing mycorrhizal carbon allocation across U.S. forests and global change scenarios. Testing mechanisms of how mycorrhizal associations affect forest soil carbon and nitrogen cycling. Dataset. doi:10.15485/2998004

dataset.name: Myco-CORPSE simulations assessing mycorrhizal carbon allocation across U.S. forests and global change scenarios
description: Plants allocate a substantial portion of their fixed carbon belowground to mycorrhizal fungi in exchange for nutrients and other benefits. However, most current ecosystem models omit mycorrhizal processes, limiting our ability to predict plant–soil carbon dynamics under environmental change. To address this gap, we used a mycorrhiza-explicit soil biogeochemical model, Myco-CORPSE (Mycorrhizal Carbon, Organisms, Rhizosphere, and Protection in the Soil Environment), to simulate tree carbon allocation to arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) and ectomycorrhizal (ECM) fungi in temperate forests.
The dataset includes outputs from two sets of model simulations:

1. Perturbation experiments: Simulations across gradients of ECM dominance (0–100%), nitrogen deposition, soil temperature, and net primary productivity (NPP) to test how these factors affect mycorrhizal C allocation and nutrient cycling.

2. FIA-based simulations: Model applications to over 1,800 U.S. forest sites using site-specific data from the U.S. Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA) program, including vegetation composition, mycorrhizal type, climate, litter traits, soil properties, and N deposition.

Model outputs include simulated mycorrhizal carbon allocation and related biogeochemical variables, such as soil and microbial carbon and nitrogen stocks. Data are provided in CSV format and organized by experiment type (in separate ZIP files). Python scripts for running simulations, plotting, and spatial mapping are also included and organized similarly. No proprietary software is required. These outputs support a peer-reviewed study and were used to generate figures and tables in the associated publication.

measurementTechnique:
Perturbation Experiments
Overview:
We conducted a set of model simulations using Myco-CORPSE, a mycorrhiza-explicit soil biogeochemical model (Shao et al., 2023), to test how global change drivers and mycorrhizal dominance influence mycorrhizal carbon (C) costs. The model simulates plant nitrogen (N) stress, mycorrhizal nutrient acquisition, and plant C allocation to arbuscular (AM) and ectomycorrhizal (ECM) fungi based on environmental conditions.
Experimental Design:
Simulations covered 66 scenarios by varying the following parameters:
• ECM dominance: 0–100% in 10% increments
• Nitrogen deposition: low (0.5 g N m⁻² yr⁻¹) and high (1.5 g N m⁻² yr⁻¹)
• Soil temperature: 5°C and 20°C
• Net Primary Productivity (NPP): 500 and 1000 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹
Model Run Setup:
Each simulation was run for 2500 years using an annual timestep, followed by 500 years using a monthly timestep to reach steady state. Model outputs were averaged over the final 50 years.
Input Parameters:
Litter stoichiometry, soil texture, and moisture were fixed to represent typical temperate forest conditions. See the “Perturbation_Myco-CORPSE.zip” file for complete input files, model configuration, and scripts.
Output Files:
Simulated outputs include mycorrhizal C allocation (as % of NPP), soil C and N stocks, and other biogeochemical variables. Results are provided in CSV format under separate folders grouped by global change driver (Climate, Ndep, NPP), bundled within the “Perturbation results.zip” archive.
Reference:
Zhu, K., McCormack, M. L., Lankau, R. A., Egan, J. F., & Wurzburger, N. (2018). Association of ectomycorrhizal trees with high carbon‐to‐nitrogen ratio soils across temperate forests is driven by smaller nitrogen not larger carbon stocks. Journal of Ecology, 106(2), 524–535. https://doi.org/10.1111/1365-2745.12918

FIA-Based Simulations
Overview:
We applied the Myco-CORPSE model to 1,825 sites from the U.S. Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA) database across the eastern United States to examine patterns of carbon (C) allocation to mycorrhizal fungi in real-world forests.
Input Data Source
All input files described below are stored in FIA_final.csv under Myco-CORPSE_FIA.zip.
• FIA tree species composition and mycorrhizal association:
The FIA program monitors forest resources across the United States using a fixed grid of permanent plots (~1 plot per 2,428 hectares), located in areas with at least 10% forest cover. Each plot includes four subplots, where trees with DBH ≥12.7 cm are recorded; smaller trees are sampled in nested microplots. We used data collected between 2000 and 2006 from fully forested, non-plantation plots. Tree species data, including basal area, were paired with literature-derived mycorrhizal associations (AM vs. EcM) to calculate the proportion of AM- or EcM-associated trees in each plot. This information was used to parameterize mycorrhizal input to Myco-CORPSE.
• Climate data:
Monthly soil temperature and moisture in the top 0–10 cm were extracted from GLDAS Noah model outputs at 0.25° × 0.25° resolution (Rodell et al., 2004). Thirty-year climatologies (1980–2009) were used.
• Soil texture:
Extracted from the Harmonized World Soil Database (HWSD v1.2) at 0.5° × 0.5° resolution (Wieder et al., 2014).
• Nitrogen deposition:
Mean annual N deposition was derived from the National Atmospheric Deposition Program (NADP) datasets over 2000–2009.
• Net Primary Production (NPP):
We used 2000–2009 data from the VPM-GPP dataset, which applies an improved light-use efficiency algorithm and is driven by MODIS and NCEP Reanalysis II data (Zhang et al., 2017). NPP was assumed to be 50% of GPP to account for autotrophic respiration.
• Plant litter traits:
Litter inputs were divided into four categories (one AM-associated and three ECM-associated groups), based on litter decomposition constants (k) and C:N ratios from tree species data in Hicks Pries et al. (2023).
Model Setup
Each site was parameterized based on species composition (mapped to AM/EcM types), climate, soil texture, litter quality, and nitrogen deposition. Simulations were run for 2,500 years of annual timesteps followed by 500 years of monthly time steps. Outputs were averaged over the final 50 years to represent steady-state conditions. See Python scripts in Myco-CORPSE_FIA.zip for full model setup.
Output Files
Simulated variables include:
• Mycorrhizal carbon allocation (% of NPP)
• Soil and microbial C and N stocks
• Nitrogen mineralization rates
• Other biogeochemical fluxes
All output data are stored in FIA_NPP%.csv under Myco-CORPSE_FIA.zip. Plotting and mapping scripts are provided in FIA_plotting.zip and FIA_mapping.zip.
